title: Proton pump inhibitors alter specific taxa in the human gastrointestinal microbiome: a crossover trial
authors: Freedberg DE, Toussaint NC, Chen SP, Ratner AJ, Whittier S, Wang TC, et al.
followUp: 4 weeks baseline, 4 or 8 weeks of omeprazole
population: Healthy volunteers in an open-label crossover trial, each serving as own control: 2 baseline faecal samples 4 weeks apart, then omeprazole 40 mg twice daily for 4 weeks (6 volunteers for 8 weeks)
funder: DEF was funded by the National Center for Advancing Translational Sciences (NIH KL2 TR000081). HHW was funded by the NIH Director's Early Independence Award (1DP5OD009172-02) and the National Science Foundation CAREER Award (MCB-1453219). SPC was funded by the Columbia University's Medical Scientist Training Program. The funding agencies had no role in the study design; the collection, analysis, or interpretation of the data; the writing of the article; or the decision to submit it for publication.
result: No significant within-individual change in microbiome diversity, but increases during PPI use in taxa associated with C. difficile infection (Enterococcaceae, Streptococcaceae) and with bacterial overgrowth (Micrococcaceae, Staphylococcaceae), a decrease in Clostridiales, unchanged faecal bile acids and an increase in bacterial invasion genes.
